value.title: PRD 002: seat bookmarks
value.summary: A seat can save a named bookmark to a file and line with a one-line note, list its bookmarks, and delete one. Bookmarks outlive a daemon restart, and listing them costs no process launches.

sections.name: why
sections.value: Seats keep losing track of places in the code they meant to come back to. A seat notices something worth revisiting mid-task, carries on, and by the time it is free the location is gone from its context, often after a compaction or a daemon restart. Today the only record is whatever the seat happens to write in its own transcript.

value.name: seat
value.need: Mark a file and line to come back to, and find it again later in the same session or after a restart.

value.name: operator
value.need: Bookmarks that cost nothing to read, so seats can list them as often as they like without loading the machine.

value.goal: A seat can get back to a place it marked earlier without re-searching the code.

value.text: Following code as it moves. A bookmark records a path and line at save time; it does not track edits that shift the line.
Sharing bookmarks between seats. Each seat sees only its own.
Editor or UI integration. Bookmarks are read and written through pij only.
Editing a bookmark in place. To change one, delete it and save it again.

value.title: Save a bookmark
value.statement: A seat saves a bookmark with a name, a file path, a line number and a one-line note, and pij confirms it was saved.
value.done_when: A seat saves bookmark `retry-loop` at `src/net.rs:120` with a note, and the next list shows that name, path, line and note.

value.title: List own bookmarks
value.statement: A seat lists its bookmarks and sees each one's name, file path, line and note, and none belonging to other seats.
value.done_when: Two seats each save one bookmark; each seat's list shows exactly its own one.

value.title: Delete a bookmark
value.statement: A seat deletes one of its bookmarks by name, and it no longer appears in that seat's list.
value.done_when: A seat with bookmarks `a` and `b` deletes `a`; its list then shows only `b`, and deleting `a` again reports that no such bookmark exists.

value.title: Survive a daemon restart
value.statement: Bookmarks saved before the daemon restarts are still listed for the same seat after it comes back.
value.done_when: A seat saves a bookmark, the daemon is restarted, and the seat's list still shows that bookmark unchanged.

value.title: Listing launches nothing
value.statement: Listing bookmarks launches no process; it is answered from in-process state or a file read.
value.done_when: A seat lists its bookmarks ten times in a row and the daemon's spawn counter does not move.

value.question: What is the command shape?
value.default: `pij bookmark add <name> <path>:<line> --note <text>`, `pij bookmark list`, `pij bookmark rm <name>`.

value.question: What happens when a seat saves a name it already has?
value.default: Refuse with a message naming the existing bookmark; the seat deletes it first if it means to replace it.

value.question: What happens to a seat's bookmarks when the seat closes?
value.default: Kept, keyed by seat id, until deleted; no automatic expiry in this PRD.

value.question: Does save check that the file and line exist?
value.default: No. The path and line are stored as given, so a bookmark can point at a file another seat is about to create.
